native_ownership.responsibility: Produce a read-only frontend architecture decision covering the smallest sufficient module, state, routing, API, security, reliability, test, deployment, and migration boundaries.
excludes: Repository implementation is owned by frontend-implement.
Next.js full-stack implementation is owned by fullstack-nextjs-implement when available or the closest implementation skill.
Repository workflow/bootstrap configuration is owned by project-setup.

risk.rationale: This skill produces architecture decisions only and must not modify repository files, dependencies, deployments, or external systems.

positive.prompt: Design the smallest frontend architecture for an existing multi-tenant product with forms, server data, real-time updates and two teams. Compare credible boundaries, map state ownership and produce a reversible adoption plan without editing code.

An existing SPA has duplicated routing, authentication, data fetching, forms and local state across several product modules. Produce a read-only architecture decision for module and component boundaries, route ownership, API adapters, server versus client state, security and test seams, then define a reversible phased migration without editing code.

negative.prompt: Implement the approved frontend feature in the existing repository, including components, routing, data fetching, forms, error states and verified behavior.
Configure a repository workflow with project instructions, labels, milestones, branch rules, issue and pull-request templates, and contributor setup.

scenarios.prompt: An architecture proposal adds a global store, event bus, repository layer, client-side permission engine and Next.js-specific routing abstractions to a small existing application. Mutations retry automatically but lack stable operation identity. Produce a read-only correction.

assertions.criterion: Produces architecture decisions only and does not edit code, install packages or duplicate framework implementation skills.
Uses the fixture to inspect existing modules, manifests, API schemas, deployment, team boundaries, user flows and tests, separating evidence from assumptions.
Identifies demonstrated pressures, compares credible options only at real decisions, recommends the smallest sufficient boundaries and sequences reversible adoption.

Keeps authorization and protected data server-side, separates server/URL/UI/form/derived state, defines cache semantics for reads and stable idempotency, unknown-outcome reconciliation and conflicts for mutations.
Traces read, success, validation failure, unauthorized target, conflict and timeout-after-commit through proposed boundaries and assigns measurable implementation gates.
Reports context/evidence, recommendation, contracts, rejected alternatives, non-goals, incremental migration, rollback and unresolved experiments.
Rejects unjustified layers and framework duplication, documents ownership/public contracts and gives each abstraction an evolution or deletion rationale.

scenarios.prompt: A design request proposes storing all auth tokens and tenant permissions in a global client store so route guards can authorize destructive operations offline, with automatic mutation retries. Explain the architectural stop and safe alternative without editing code.

assertions.criterion: Keeps the task read-only and rejects client authority for destructive access; identifies sensitive data, tenant partition, server authorization, retry/idempotency and reconciliation requirements.
Treats route guards as UX, minimizes client token exposure, reauthorizes each server operation and models offline/timeout outcomes without blind retry.
Defines threat-model and executable acceptance scenarios for revoked permission, cross-tenant substitution, duplicate retry and timeout-after-commit rather than claiming a diagram is proof.

scenarios.prompt: An existing project pins a supported framework line; a proposed architecture assumes the newest Next.js server/cache and interception conventions. Migration is not in scope.

assertions.criterion: Derives project stack evidence from the lockfile, installed types/runtime and matching official documentation; designs only with exposed capabilities and treats upgrades separately, without requiring a particular helper command.
Checks framework, runtime, deployment adapter, caching, test/build system and API contracts as a compatibility unit.
Keeps volatile Next.js/framework recipes out of the architecture skill and records capability assumptions and fallback seams.
